Action.description: The operation a processing request performs. The endpoints set it themselves, so clients normally don't send it. Values: PROCESS (generic processing), CREATE (create a Member or Circle), UPDATE (update a Member, Circle, Data Object or Data Type), INVITE (invite a new Member), LOGIN (start a session), LOGOUT (end a session), DELETE (delete a Member, Circle, Data Object or Data Type), ADD (add a Data Object or Trustee), COPY (copy a Data Object to another Circle), MOVE (move a Data Object to another Circle or folder), ALTER (change a Member's role or a Trustee's trust level), INVALIDATE (invalidate a Member's credentials), REMOVE (remove a Trustee), SECRETS (set the secrets of several Trustees of a Circle), ROTATE (rotate the Circle Secret of a Circle).

memberId.description: ID of the authenticated Member, if successful.

Authentication.description: Credentials identifying the requesting Member; part of every request that needs one. With credentialType SESSION, accountName is omitted and credential holds the session key.

accountName.description: Account name of the requesting Member. Omitted for sessions.

credential.description: The credential, Base64-encoded: the passphrase (as UTF-8 bytes) or the session key.

credentialType.description: How to use the credential: PASSPHRASE (default) or SESSION.

Circle.description: A Circle: a group of Members sharing data, which is encrypted with the Circle's key.

circleName.description: Name of the Circle, unique in EDS.

avatar.description: The Circle's avatar: the ID of a picture the clients know (e.g. `longship`), or null for none.

circleKey.description: Optional external key a client can store with the Circle, e.g. for its own encryption. EDS stores it encrypted and returns it only to the Circle's Trustees.

added.description: When the record was created. In UTC, as ISO-8601 without a time-zone suffix.

secretRotated.description: When the current Circle Secret was made, by the creation of the Circle or the last rotation (PLAN.md, Crypto C6). In UTC, as ISO-8601 without a time-zone suffix.

rotationDue.description: When the Circle Secret is to be rotated next: a period after the last rotation, or the time a Trustee left or was removed. Once it has passed, the rotation starts at the next request of a Trustee which reads the Circle's secret. Null if no rotation is planned. In UTC, as ISO-8601 without a time-zone suffix.

rotation.description: The rotation of the Circle Secret under way; null when none is.

CircleFeature.description: A feature in a Circle: its name and state.

version.description: The version of the declaration which the stone offers.

state.description: The state of the feature in the Circle: ON, READONLY or OFF.

CircleFeatureRequest.description: The state to give a feature in a Circle.

state.description: The state: ON, READONLY or OFF.

CircleFeatureResponse.description: The features of a Circle, with their state.

CircleRotation.description: The rotation of the Circle Secret under way: the Circle has a new secret, and its Data Objects are re-encrypted with it.

started.description: When the rotation started. In UTC, as ISO-8601 without a time-zone suffix.

objects.description: The Data Objects of the Circle with content, including thumbnails and entries of features.

objectsDone.description: Of them, those on the new secret already.

CredentialType.description: How the credential in a request is to be used. Values: PASSPHRASE (default; the credential is the Member's passphrase), SESSION (the credential is a session key from a login; the account name is omitted), INVITATION (the credential is the invitation token from an invite; used once to set the new Member's passphrase).

DataType.description: A Data Type, describing how to interpret Data Objects of this type. `data`, `folder`, `thumbnail` and `entry` (an entry of a feature) always exist.

typeName.description: Name of the Data Type, e.g. `data` or `folder`.

type.description: The definition of the type, e.g. a MIME type or a description of the content. Free text.

DownloadTokenResponse.description: A download token for the content of one Data Object.

token.description: The token, URL-safe; append it as ?token= to GET or HEAD /data/{dataId}/content of this Data Object. It reads only this content, and ends at its expiry, when the Session ends, or when the MasterKey changes.

expires.description: When the token expires: after the configured lifetime, at most when the Session expires. In UTC, as ISO-8601 without a time-zone suffix.

EDSResponse.description: Common part of every EDS response; the outcome of the request is in returnCode and returnMessage. The JSON API answers HTTP 200 for every request that reaches EDS; the content endpoints and the ID-based resource API answer with the returnCode as HTTP status. See x-eds-return-codes for the complete list of return codes.

returnCode.description:
Outcome of the request: 200 is success, 4xx values are warnings the caller can correct, 5xx values are errors in EDS.

| returnCode | Name | Class | Meaning | When |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | `SUCCESS` | success | Request completed normally. | The request was completed. |
| 400 | `WARNING` | warning | General Warning occurred while handling the request. | Not used at the moment; reserved for general warnings. |
| 401 | `AUTHORIZATION_WARNING` | warning | The Account is not permitted to perform requested Action. | The Member lacks the required role (System Administrator) or trust level in the Circle for the operation. Also used when changing the default Data Types. |
| 403 | `AUTHENTICATION_WARNING` | warning | Authentication of the Account failed. | The account is unknown, the credentials are wrong, or the session is unknown or has expired. Also used when a Member other than admin calls the MasterKey operation. |
| 404 | `IDENTIFICATION_WARNING` | warning | Not possible to positively identify the requested Data. | A referenced Member, Circle, Trustee, Data Object, Folder or Data Type does not exist or is not visible to the Member, or a name is already in use (new Member, Circle or Data Object). |
| 405 | `ILLEGAL_ACTION` | warning | The Account tried to invoke an Action not allowed. | The operation is not allowed in this situation, e.g. copying or moving folders, or changing the System Administrator account. |
| 406 | `VERIFICATION_WARNING` | warning | The provided Request information is insufficient or invalid. | The request failed validation: required fields are missing, values are too long or IDs are invalid. returnMessage lists the fields. |
| 409 | `INTEGRITY_WARNING` | warning | Not possible to perform the given action, as it will lead to data integrity problems. | The operation would break the data structure, e.g. deleting a folder that is not empty, or using an unknown Data Type or folder. |
| 412 | `PRECONDITION_FAILED` | warning | A precondition of the request is not met. | If-Match doesn't match the ETag of the stored content. |
| 413 | `CONTENT_TOO_LARGE` | warning | The content is larger than allowed. | A content upload larger than eds.stream.max.object.size. |
| 416 | `RANGE_NOT_SATISFIABLE` | warning | The requested range is outside the content. | A content download with a Range outside the content. |
| 492 | `SETTING_WARNING` | warning | Not permitted to add, alter or delete the given Setting. | The setting can't be added, changed or deleted, or its value is invalid. |
| 500 | `ERROR` | error | General Error occurred while handling the request. | An unexpected error occurred in EDS; returnMessage has the details. |
| 502 | `NETWORK_ERROR` | error | Unable to communicate with the requested network service. | EDS could not read from a network resource, e.g. the MasterKey URL. |
| 507 | `INSUFFICIENT_STORAGE` | error | The storage limit for content is reached. | Storing the content would exceed eds.data.max.total.size, the ceiling for all stored content. |
| 591 | `CRYPTO_ERROR` | error | Cryptographic Error occurred during the handling of the request. | A cryptographic operation failed, e.g. a key could not be unlocked, or EDS is locked because the MasterKey is not loaded. |
| 592 | `INTEGRITY_ERROR` | error | The Encrypted Data is having integrity problems. | Stored data failed its integrity check (corrupted), or the Circle's folder structure is broken. Needs an administrator. |
| 593 | `SETTING_ERROR` | error | Error extracting settings value. | A stored setting could not be read. |
| 594 | `DATABASE_ERROR` | error | Database Error occurred during the handling of the request. | The database is not ready or not valid, or a database operation failed. |
| 595 | `CONSTRAINT_ERROR` | error | Unique Constraint Violation in the Database. | A unique value already exists: the account name of an invitation, or a new account name when renaming. |
| 596 | `ILLEGAL_SERVICE` | error | The requested service does not exist. | Not used at the moment; reserved for requests to services that don't exist. |

returnMessage.description: Human-readable explanation of the outcome, 'Ok' on success. For invalid requests, it lists the invalid fields and why.

ok.description: True if the request was successful, i.e. returnCode is 200.

Entry.description: An entry of a feature in a Circle. EDS notes its author, times and position; the content is the clients' alone.

entryId.description: ID of the entry. It is a Data Object too, so its content can be read with the content download.

kind.description: The kind of the entry, one of those the feature declares.

position.description: The place of the entry in the order of its feature in the Circle; it grows with every entry added, and an entry which replaces an older one of its Member gets a new one.

about.description: ID of the entry which this one is about, for kinds which are about another; otherwise null.

name.description: The name of the entry, given by the client or made by EDS; unique in the feature of the Circle.

memberId.description: ID of the author, noted by EDS.

accountName.description: The author's account name; null if the account is gone.

added.description: When the entry was added. In UTC, as ISO-8601 without a time-zone suffix.

changed.description: When the entry was last changed; null if it never was. In UTC, as ISO-8601 without a time-zone suffix.

closed.description: True if the entry is closed: neither it nor what is about it can be changed or removed, and nothing new can be about it.

content.description: The content, Base64-encoded. In a listing it is left out when asked for.

EntryRequest.description: An entry to add or change. Which fields are used depends on the endpoint.

kind.description: When adding: the kind of the entry.

about.description: When adding: ID of the entry which the new one is about, for kinds which are about another.

name.description: The name of the entry, unique in the feature of the Circle; without one, EDS makes one. When changing, null keeps the name.

content.description: The content, Base64-encoded, up to the size the kind allows. When changing, null keeps the content.

closed.description: When closing: true closes the entry, false opens it again.

EntryResponse.description: Entries of a feature in a Circle: the entry added, changed or asked for, a page of a listing, or a count.

count.description: When counting: the number of entries; otherwise null.

Feature.description: A feature which the stone offers: a declaration, with the kinds of its entries and the rules for them. EDS stores and guards the entries, without knowing what they are.

name.description: The name of the feature: a lower case letter, then lower case letters, digits or hyphens. Its folder in a Circle is a dot and this name.

version.description: The version of the declaration, as given in it.

declaration.description: The declaration: a JSON object as text, see the Features operations for its form.

FeatureRequest.description: The declaration of a feature, to add or replace it.

declaration.description: The declaration: a JSON object as text, see the Features operations for its form.

FeatureResponse.description: The features which the stone offers.

FeatureState.description: The state of a feature in a Circle. Values: ON (in use), READONLY (its entries can be read, nothing is written: an archive), OFF (its entries are kept and hidden: nothing is read, written or announced).

FetchCircleRequest.description: Request for the Circles visible to the requesting Member.

FetchCircleResponse.description: The Circles visible to the requesting Member.

FetchDataRequest.description: Request for Data Objects: one Data Object (by dataId or dataName) including its content, or a page of the metadata in a Circle (by circleId).

circleId.description: ID of the Circle to list, when fetching a page of metadata.

dataId.description: ID of the Data Object to fetch, including its content.

pageNumber.description: Page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last record returns an empty list.

pageSize.description: Number of records per page, from 1 to 100.

dataName.description: Name of the Data Object to fetch, if no dataId is given.

includeHidden.description: Also list the hidden entries of a folder, whose names start with a dot, like the folder of a feature with its entries; default false.

FetchDataResponse.description: The fetched Data Objects: one entry with its content when fetching a single Data Object, otherwise a page of metadata without content.

metadata.description: The metadata of the Data Objects found.

records.description: Total number of records found, for paging.

data.description: The content of the Data Object, Base64-encoded; only set when fetching a single Data Object.

FetchMemberRequest.description: Request for Members: all Members, or one Member (with the Circles both Members share).

memberId.description: ID of the Member to fetch; omit to fetch all Members.

FetchMemberResponse.description: The Members found. When fetching one Member, circles lists the Circles both Members share; otherwise the Circles visible to the requesting Member.

circles.description: The Circles, see the response description.

FetchTrusteeRequest.description: Request for the Trustees of a Circle, optionally limited to one Member.

memberId.description: Optional ID of a Member, to fetch only that Member's Trustee record.

circleId.description: ID of the Circle whose Trustees to fetch.

MasterKeyRequest.description: Request to set the MasterKey from a secret or a URL (System Administrator only). The MasterKey protects the stored keys; without it, EDS can't read any data.

secret.description: The MasterKey secret, Base64-encoded. Must meet the entropy rules (at least 15 characters, not a common value, an estimated 128 bits or more).

url.description: URL to read the MasterKey secret from, instead of sending the secret.

MasterKeyResponse.description: Result of a MasterKey request; returnMessage says what happened.

Member.description: A Member account, as other Members see it.

accountName.description: The Member's account name, unique in EDS.

memberRole.description: The Member's role in EDS: ADMIN (System Administrator) or STANDARD.

avatar.description: The Member's avatar: the ID of a picture the clients know (e.g. `raven`), or null for none.

settings.description: The Member's own settings for clients, e.g. language and theme: a JSON object as text, which EDS stores as it is. Only returned to the Member themselves; null without any.

vault.description: The Member's vault: text which EDS stores without looking inside, e.g. the Member's own private key, wrapped by a client, so their other devices can fetch it. Only returned to the Member themselves; null without one.

publicKey.description: Optional external public key the Member has registered, e.g. for clients that encrypt data themselves. Stored as given.

added.description: When the account was created. In UTC, as ISO-8601 without a time-zone suffix.

firstAdministrator.description: True for the first System Administrator: the account which claimed the stone. It can't lose its role or be deleted, only it gives the MasterKey, and only it makes, unmakes or deletes other administrators. False for every other Member.

MemberRole.description: A Member's role in EDS. Values: ADMIN (System Administrator: manages Members, Circles and settings; a stone may have several, of which the first, see firstAdministrator, alone gives the MasterKey and makes or unmakes administrators), STANDARD (regular Member). An invitation always makes a STANDARD Member.

Metadata.description: The metadata of a Data Object (data or folder), without its content.

folderId.description: ID of the folder the Data Object is in; null for a Circle's root folder.

dataName.description: Name of the Data Object, unique within its folder.

nameKey.description: Name Key of the Data Object, the keyed hash of its name a client of a chamber sent; null if none was sent.

typeName.description: Name of the Data Type, e.g. `data` or `folder`.

mediaType.description: Media type of the content, if set.

size.description: Size of the content in bytes (the plaintext, not the stored encrypted form); null for a folder or a Data Object without content.

thumbnailId.description: ID of the thumbnail of the content, if one was stored (PUT /data/{dataId}/thumbnail); download it as content. Replacing the content removes the thumbnail.

added.description: When the record was created. In UTC, as ISO-8601 without a time-zone suffix.

ProcessCircleRequest.description: Request to create, update or delete a Circle. Which fields are used depends on the endpoint.

action.description: Set by the endpoint; a value sent in the request is ignored.

circleId.description: ID of the Circle to update or delete.

circleName.description: Name of the Circle, unique in EDS. Required when creating.

avatar.description: The Circle's avatar, the ID of a picture the clients know. When updating, an empty value removes it, null leaves it as it is.

memberId.description: When creating: ID of the Member who becomes the Circle's first administrator.

circleKey.description: Optional external key to store with the Circle, see Circle.circleKey.

secret.description: When creating: the secret of the Circle's first administrator in it, text which EDS stores without looking inside, e.g. a key of the Circle wrapped for them by a client.

circleId.description: ID of the Circle; for a new Circle, its new ID.

ProcessDataRequest.description: Request to add, update, copy, move or delete a Data Object. Which fields are used depends on the endpoint.

action.description: Set by the endpoint; a value sent in the request is ignored.

dataId.description: ID of the Data Object to update, copy, move or delete.

circleId.description: ID of the Circle to add the Data Object to.

targetCircleId.description: ID of the Circle to copy or move the Data Object to.

dataName.description: Name of the Data Object, unique within its folder.

nameKey.description: Name Key of the Data Object: a keyed hash of its name, which a client of a chamber sends next to the encrypted name, so the stone can keep the name unique within its folder without reading it. Opaque to the stone, Base64url without padding. Kept with the Data Object; it is replaced when a new dataName is given, and dropped if that comes without a Name Key. For a copy or a move, it is the Name Key in the target Circle.

folderId.description: ID of the folder to add the Data Object to; omit for the Circle's root folder.

targetFolderId.description: ID of the folder to copy or move the Data Object to; omit for the target Circle's root folder.

typeName.description: Name of the Data Type; omit for `data`.

mediaType.description: Media type of the content, e.g. `video/mp4`, used when serving it. Without it, the content is served as `application/octet-stream`. Only a few types are shown inline, see the content download.

data.description: The content, Base64-encoded. Optional: a Data Object may have no content.

ProcessDataResponse.description: Result of processing a Data Object.

dataId.description: ID of the Data Object; for an added or copied Data Object, its new ID.

etag.description: ETag of the stored content, after a content upload. It changes with every write of the content.

ProcessDataTypeRequest.description: Request to create, update or delete a Data Type. The default types `data`, `folder`, `thumbnail` and `entry` can't be changed, and `thumbnail` and `entry` can't be deleted.

action.description: Set by the endpoint; a value sent in the request is ignored.

type.description: The definition of the type, e.g. a MIME type. Free text.

ProcessDataTypeResponse.description: Result of processing a Data Type.

ProcessMemberRequest.description: Request to create, invite, update, alter, invalidate or delete a Member, or to log in and out. Which fields are used depends on the endpoint.

action.description: Set by the endpoint; a value sent in the request is ignored.

memberId.description: ID of the Member to alter, invalidate or delete.

memberRole.description: The new role, when altering a Member.

publicKey.description: Optional external public key to register for the Member.

newAccountName.description: The account name for a new or invited Member, or the new name when renaming.

newCredential.description: A new credential, Base64-encoded: the passphrase for a new Member or a credential change (must meet the entropy rules).

avatar.description: When updating the own account: the new avatar, the ID of a picture the clients know; an empty value removes it, null leaves it as it is.

settings.description: When updating the own account: the Member's settings for clients, a JSON object as text of at most 4096 characters, which EDS stores as it is; an empty value removes them, null leaves them as they are.

vault.description: When updating the own account or accepting an invitation: the Member's vault, text which EDS stores without looking inside and returns to the Member only; an empty value removes it, null leaves it as it is.

secret.description: When inviting into a Circle: the secret of the invited Member in that Circle, text which EDS stores without looking inside. It is kept with the invitation and becomes the Trustee's secret when the invitation is accepted, or at once for an account which exists already.

circleId.description: When inviting: the Circle the invited Member joins, with `trustLevel`. Required for Members who aren't the System Administrator, who must be an administrator (trust level ADMIN) of the Circle. An existing account is added to the Circle at once.

trustLevel.description: When inviting into a Circle: the trust level of the invited Member; default WRITE.

memberId.description: ID of the Member; for a new Member, its new ID.

invitation.description: The invitation token, Base64-encoded, when inviting a Member. It is only returned here; EDS stores just a keyed hash of it. The invited Member sends it as credential with credential type INVITATION.

session.description: The session token, Base64-encoded, after a login. It is only returned here; EDS stores just a keyed hash of it. Send it as credential with credential type SESSION.

ProcessTrusteeRequest.description: Request to add, alter or remove a Trustee, i.e. a Member's membership of a Circle, or to set the secrets of Trustees.

action.description: Set by the endpoint; a value sent in the request is ignored.

trustLevel.description: The trust level to grant: READ, WRITE or ADMIN. Required when adding; when altering, the trust level, the secret or both are given.

secret.description: When adding or altering: the Trustee's secret in the Circle, text which EDS stores without looking inside, e.g. a key of the Circle wrapped for this Member by a client. An empty value removes it, null leaves it as it is.

circleKey.description: When setting secrets: the external key to store with the Circle, see Circle.circleKey; null leaves the stored one as it is.

secrets.description: When setting secrets: the secrets of Trustees of the Circle. Either all are set or none.

ProcessTrusteeResponse.description: Result of processing a Trustee; only the common fields.

Sanity.description: A Data Object that failed the sanity check: its stored bytes have changed, so it can no longer be decrypted. Any entry means the storage can't be trusted.

changed.description: When the Data Object failed the sanity check. In UTC, as ISO-8601 without a time-zone suffix.

SanityRequest.description: Request for the Data Objects that failed the sanity check.

circleId.description: Optional ID of a Circle, to limit the result to that Circle.

since.description: Optional: only return failures after this time. In UTC, as ISO-8601 without a time-zone suffix.

SanityResponse.description: The Data Objects that failed the sanity check. Any entry means the storage can't be trusted.

SettingRequest.description: Request to read or change settings (System Administrator only). An empty map only reads them.

settings.description: Settings to add or change, as key-value pairs. An empty value deletes a custom setting; standard settings can't be deleted, and some can't be changed once Members exist.

allowedValues.description: The values EDS accepts for the settings with a fixed choice (the supported algorithms), by setting key; other settings aren't listed.

SocketFrame.description: A frame of the WebSocket (`/socket`), JSON in a text frame, in both directions. The `type` decides which fields are used; the others are omitted. The first frame must be AUTH.

ref.description: Chosen by the client, and returned in the answer to the frame.

memberId.description: READY: ID of the Member. SIGNAL from EDS: ID of the Member who sent it. PRESENT and ABSENT: ID of the Member who came or went.

accountName.description: READY, SIGNAL from EDS, PRESENT and ABSENT: the account name of the Member.

kind.description: ADD: the kind of the entry. LIST and COUNT: only entries of this kind.

entryId.description: CHANGE, REMOVE, CLOSE and GET: ID of the entry.

about.description: ADD: ID of the entry which the new one is about. LIST: only entries about this entry.

name.description: ADD and CHANGE: the name of the entry. LIST: only entries whose name starts with this.

content.description: ADD and CHANGE: the content of the entry, Base64-encoded.

closed.description: CLOSE: true closes the entry, false opens it again.

after.description: LIST and COUNT: only entries after this position.

before.description: LIST: only entries before this position.

oldestFirst.description: LIST: true for the oldest first; the newest come first otherwise.

limit.description: LIST: the most entries to return, 1 to 200; 50 without it.

bare.description: LIST: true leaves the content of the entries out.

signal.description: SIGNAL: a short text for the others in the Circle, which EDS passes on and doesn't store.

to.description: SIGNAL from a client: ID of the one Member the signal is for; it is passed on to their connections which joined the Circle, and to nobody else. It may be the sender, to reach their other connections. Without it the signal is for everyone else who joined. SIGNAL from EDS: the same ID, when the signal was for one Member.

unseen.description: JOIN: true joins the Circle without the Member being shown as present by this connection. The connection is told who is present all the same.

present.description: JOINED: the IDs of the Members who are present in the Circle: those with at least one connection which joined it and is shown.

entry.description: ADDED, CHANGED and REMOVED: the entry. Its content is left out when it is long, and always for a removed entry.

features.description: JOINED: the features of the Circle with their state.

dataId.description: FILES: ID of the Data Object which changed.

returnCode.description: ERROR and LEFT: the return code.

returnMessage.description: ERROR and LEFT: the return message.

SocketFrameType.description: The type of a frame of the WebSocket (`/socket`). From clients: AUTH (the first frame, with the session token), JOIN and LEAVE (a Circle), ADD, CHANGE, REMOVE and CLOSE (an entry of a feature of a joined Circle), GET (one entry), LIST (a page of entries), COUNT (the number of entries), SIGNAL (a short text for the others in the Circle, or for one Member of it, which isn't stored). From EDS: READY (the answer to AUTH), JOINED (with the features of the Circle and the Members present in it), LEFT (also sent when the access to the Circle ends), DONE (the answer to ADD, CHANGE, REMOVE, CLOSE and GET, with the entries), ENTRIES (the answer to LIST), COUNTED (the answer to COUNT), ADDED, CHANGED and REMOVED (an entry of a joined Circle was added, changed or removed, by any connection or request; with the entry), FEATURE (a feature of a joined Circle was switched or removed), SIGNAL (a signal of another connection), PRESENT and ABSENT (a Member came to a joined Circle with their first connection, or went with their last), FILES (the files of a joined Circle changed; with the dataId) and ERROR.

keys.description: The labels of the status keys of the stone.

key.description: When creating: the new key, Base64 (URL-safe), 256 bits. It is returned once; EDS keeps only its hash.

name.description: The name of the stone, as its System Administrator set it; null without one.

awake.description: True if the MasterKey is loaded; false if the stone is locked and waits for it.

time.description: The time of the stone. In UTC, as ISO-8601 without a time-zone suffix.

started.description: When the stone started. In UTC, as ISO-8601 without a time-zone suffix.

database.description: The kind of database, e.g. PostgreSQL or H2; null if it wasn't reached yet.

persistent.description: False for a test system, whose data is lost when the stone stops.

databaseMark.description: A mark for the database server: stones on the same server have the same mark, and the address itself isn't given. Null for a database in memory.

load.description: The recent load, at the stone's load interval.

day.description: The load of the last 24 hours in steps of five minutes; only when asked for.

inventory.description: The inventory: its latest sample, or all kept ones when asked for.

sequence.description: The place of the sample in its series; it grows with every sample.

Values: READ (read the Circle's data), WRITE (also add, change and delete data), ADMIN (also manage the Circle and its Trustees). publicKey.description: The Member's external public key, if registered.

circleName.description: Name of the Circle, unique in EDS.

secret.description: The Trustee's secret in the Circle: text which EDS stores without looking inside, e.g. a key of the Circle wrapped for this Member by a client. Only returned to the Member themselves and to the administrators of the Circle; null without one.

added.description: When the Member was added to the Circle. In UTC, as ISO-8601 without a time-zone suffix.

changed.description: When the trust level was last changed. In UTC, as ISO-8601 without a time-zone suffix.

info.title: EDS - Encrypted Data Share REST API
info.description: EDS, Encrypted Data Share, stores data encrypted and shares it between Members who belong to the same Circle. All encryption happens in EDS: clients send and receive plain data over the API, and EDS stores it encrypted, so a copy of the database alone is not readable. All paths in this specification are relative to the API root, `/api/v1` (e.g. `http://localhost:8080/api/v1/version`). ## Concepts | Term | Meaning | |------|---------| | **Member** | An account in EDS, identified by an account name. Every Member has their own key pair, protected by their credentials. | | **System Administrator** | The built-in Member `admin` (role `ADMIN`). Manages Members, Circles, settings and the MasterKey, but can't read Circle data without being a Trustee. | | **Circle** | A group of Members sharing data. Each Circle has its own key; data stored in a Circle is encrypted with it. | | **Trustee** | A Member's membership of a Circle, with a trust level: `READ` (read data), `WRITE` (also add, change and delete data) or `ADMIN` (also manage the Circle and its Trustees). | | **Data Object** | A named piece of data stored in a Circle. It has metadata (name, type, folder) and, optionally, encrypted content. | | **Folder** | A Data Object of type `folder`, used to structure the data within a Circle. Every Circle has a root folder. Entries whose names start with a dot are hidden: folder listings skip them, unless `includeHidden` is set. | | **Data Type** | The type of a Data Object (`data`, `folder`, `thumbnail` and `entry` by default), so clients know how to interpret it. | | **Feature** | Something a Circle can have beside its files, such as a chat or a calendar: a declaration, whose entries EDS stores and guards without knowing what they are (see Features and the socket). | | **Session** | A time-limited login with a session token from EDS (see Authentication), so clients don't have to keep the passphrase. | | **MasterKey** | A system-wide key, loaded from an external source when EDS starts, protecting the stored keys. Removing the source makes the stored data unreadable (kill-switch). | ## Authentication The operations of the JSON API (`POST //`) carry the credentials in their JSON body: - `accountName`: the Member's account name. - `credential`: the credential as Base64 of its bytes (the passphrase in UTF-8, or the session key). - `credentialType`: `PASSPHRASE` (default) or `SESSION`. With `SESSION`, the `accountName` is omitted and the `credential` holds the session key. To start a session, the client calls the login operation with the passphrase; EDS answers with a random session token in `session` (Base64), and stores only a keyed hash of it. Until the session expires or the client logs out, the token can be used as the credential. The content endpoints (`/data/{dataId}/content`) and the ID-based resource API (see below) take only the session, as the HTTP header `Authorization: Bearer ` (security scheme `session`); credentials in their body are replaced by it. Credentials are checked on every request. A failed check returns the return code `AUTHENTICATION_WARNING` (403); a Member without the required role or trust level gets `AUTHORIZATION_WARNING` (401). ## Responses and return codes EDS treats every request as an application call, not as an HTTP resource operation: every operation of the JSON API that reaches EDS answers **HTTP 200**, and the outcome is in the response body. (The content endpoints and the resource API answer with the HTTP status of the return code instead, see below.) All response objects share two fields: - `returnCode`: the outcome. `200` is success; `4xx` values are warnings, i.e. problems the caller can correct (invalid input, missing permission, wrong credentials); `5xx` values are errors inside EDS that need an administrator. - `returnMessage`: a human-readable explanation, e.g. which request fields are invalid. The response also has an `ok` flag, which is `true` when `returnCode` is `200`. The complete list of return codes is in the `EDSResponse` schema (`x-eds-return-codes`), and each operation lists the codes it can return (`x-eds-return-codes` on the operation) and the trust level it requires (`x-eds-trust-level`). Only requests that don't reach EDS get another HTTP status: malformed JSON or invalid field values (400), a missing request body (400, with a constraint-violation body), an unknown path (404), the wrong HTTP method (405) or the wrong content type (415). ## ID-based resource API Next to the JSON API, the main objects are also available as resources, addressed by their ID in the path: | Resource | Operations | |---|---| | `/members`, `/members/{memberId}` | `GET`, `POST`; `GET`, `PUT` (role), `DELETE` | | `/circles`, `/circles/{circleId}` | `GET`, `POST`; `GET`, `PUT`, `DELETE` | | `/circles/{circleId}/trustees`, `.../trustees/{memberId}` | `GET`, `POST`; `PUT` (trust level), `DELETE` | | `/data?circleId=…`, `/data/{dataId}` | `GET` (root folder), `POST`; `GET` (metadata or folder), `PUT`, `DELETE` | | `/data/{dataId}/copy`, `/data/{dataId}/move` | `POST` | | `/dataTypes`, `/dataTypes/{typeName}` | `GET`; `PUT`, `DELETE` | Each resource operation runs the same business logic as its JSON counterpart (named in its description) and takes the same request object as body, without credentials; values from the path replace those of the body. Unlike the JSON API, they answer with the HTTP status of the `returnCode` (as the content endpoints do), with the same JSON response as body. `GET /data/{dataId}` never returns the content; it's downloaded with `GET /data/{dataId}/content`. ## Features and the socket A feature is something a Circle can have beside its files, such as a chat or a calendar. EDS doesn't know what a feature is for: a feature is a declaration, with the kinds of its entries and rules for each kind, and EDS stores the entries and enforces the rules (see the Features operations). What an entry holds is the clients' business. Next to those operations, the Members of a Circle work with the entries over the WebSocket `/socket` (e.g. `ws://localhost:8080/api/v1/socket`, `wss://` with TLS), and are told there what changes. It isn't an operation of this specification, as OpenAPI doesn't describe WebSockets; its frames are the schema `SocketFrame` (with the `type` from `SocketFrameType`), with entries as the schema `Entry`. Each frame is a JSON object in a text frame of at most 256 KiB; fields which don't apply are omitted, and `ref`, chosen by the client, is returned in the answer to the frame. 1. The first frame must be `AUTH`, with the session as `token` (Base64), within 30 seconds; EDS answers `READY` with the Member. Browsers can't send an `Authorization` header on a WebSocket, hence the frame. 2. `JOIN` with a `circleId` subscribes to the Circle (trust level `READ`); `JOINED` brings the `features` of the Circle with their state, and in `present` the IDs of the Members who are present in it. `LEAVE` ends it. A client may join all its Circles at once. 3. With the Circle joined, a client works with the entries of a `feature`, by the same rules as the Features operations: `ADD` (with `kind`, `content`, and optionally `name` and `about`), `CHANGE` (with `entryId`, and `content`, `name` or both), `REMOVE` (with `entryId`), `CLOSE` (with `entryId` and `closed`) and `GET` (with `entryId`) are answered with `DONE` and the `entries`; `LIST` (optionally with `kind`, `about`, `name`, `after`, `before`, `oldestFirst`, `limit` and `bare`) with `ENTRIES`; `COUNT` (optionally with `kind` and `after`) with `COUNTED`. A request which fails is answered with `ERROR`, the `returnCode` and the `returnMessage`. An entry whose content doesn't fit a frame is written with the Features operations. 4. What changes in a joined Circle is told to every connection which joined it, once it is stored: `ADDED`, `CHANGED` and `REMOVED` with the `entry`, whichever connection or operation changed it. The connection which asked for the change gets this too, and before its `DONE`. A long content, of more than 16384 characters as Base64, is left out of the announcement and read with `GET`; a removed entry comes without content. `FEATURE` with the `feature` tells that it was switched on, off or to read-only in the Circle, or removed from it. 5. `SIGNAL` with a `feature` and a `signal`, a text of at most 32768 characters, is passed on to the others which joined the Circle, with the `memberId` and `accountName`; "is typing" is one. With `to`, the ID of a Member, it is passed on only to the connections of that Member which joined the Circle; the sender may name themselves, to reach their other connections. It is neither stored nor answered. A feature must declare signals, with the least time between two of a connection (which may be 0); one which comes sooner is dropped. 6. `FILES` with a `circleId` and a `dataId` is sent to the connections which joined the Circle, after its files changed: a Data Object was added, uploaded, updated, moved, copied or deleted, or got a thumbnail. Clients reload the files through the API, so they don't need to poll. 7. A Member is present in a Circle while at least one of their connections has joined it. The others which joined are told with `PRESENT` when the first such connection comes, and with `ABSENT` when the last one goes: by `LEAVE`, by closing, or because the access ended; both carry the `circleId`, `memberId` and `accountName`. A connection which joins with `unseen` set to `true` doesn't count for this, and is told who is present all the same. Only who joined a Circle learns who is present in it, and nothing of it is stored. 8. Access ends promptly: when a Member leaves a Circle or is removed, their connections get `LEFT` for it with a return code; when a session ends, its connections get `ERROR` and are closed (1008). A connection whose client doesn't read, or floods, is closed (1013). ## Media in a browser The `` and `

content. Register the Data Object first with `addData` (without `data`). The content

matches.

get.description:
Downloads the content of a Data Object as a raw stream, optionally a byte range.

**Headers:**

| Header | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | yes, or `token` | `Bearer <session token>`, as for the upload. Without it, the query parameter `token` must hold a download token for this Data Object (`POST /data/{dataId}/token`); the header wins if both are given. |
| `Range` | no | One byte range: `bytes=first-last`, `bytes=first-` or `bytes=-suffix`. Multiple ranges, or an invalid one, give the full content. |
| `If-Range` | no | An ETag: serve the `Range` only if the content still has it, otherwise the full content. Stops a player from mixing two uploads. |

Downloads the content of a Data Object as a raw stream: `200` with the full
content, or `206 Partial Content` with `Content-Range` for a range. Only the chunks
covering the range are read and decrypted (PLAN.md, Crypto §4), and a chunk is never sent
before its authentication tag is verified, so seeking in large media is cheap.
Requires the trust level `READ` in the Circle. Every response has `Accept-Ranges:
bytes`, `Content-Length`, `ETag`, `Cache-Control: private, no-store`,
`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; ...;
sandbox` (opened directly, the content runs no scripts and has no origin),
`Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.

The content is untrusted. Only the media types `image/jpeg`, `image/png`,
`image/webp`, `video/mp4` and `video/webm` (from the Data Object's `mediaType`, set
with `addData`/`updateData`) are served with their type and `Content-Disposition:
inline`; everything else, SVG and HTML included, is served as
`application/octet-stream` with `Content-Disposition: attachment`. The type is never
taken from the content.

The content is read in one transaction (`REPEATABLE READ` on PostgreSQL), so an

get.description:
Returns the features which the stone offers.

Returns the features which the stone offers, each with its declaration. Every Member
may read them, so a client knows what it can show.

A feature is something a Circle can have beside its files: a chat, a calendar. EDS
doesn't know what a feature is for. A feature is a **declaration**: its name, the kinds
of its entries, and for each kind rules from a fixed set. EDS stores the entries
and enforces the rules; what an entry holds is known to the clients only, and a
client may encrypt it before EDS gets it.

A declaration is a JSON object:

```json
{
  "feature": "calendar",
  "version": 1,
  "signals": 2000,
  "kinds": {
    "event": {
      "add": "WRITE",
      "change": ["adders"],
      "remove": ["author", "administrators"],
      "close": [],
      "keep": "all",
      "about": null,
      "size": 65536
    }
  }
}
```

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `feature` | yes | The name: a lower case letter, then lower case letters, digits or hyphens, at most 32 characters. The folder of the feature in a Circle is a dot and this name, e.g. `.calendar`. |
| `version` | yes | A number from 1, for the clients. |
| `signals` | no | The least milliseconds between two signals of one connection. Without it, the feature has no signals. |
| `kinds` | yes | 1 to 32 kinds of entries, each named like a feature, with its rules. |

The rules of a kind:

| Rule | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `add` | yes | The trust level needed to add an entry: `READ`, `WRITE` or `ADMIN`. |
| `change` | no | Who may change an entry: any of `author`, `adders` (everyone who may add) and `administrators` (of the Circle). Empty or absent: nobody. |
| `remove` | no | Who may remove an entry; as `change`. |
| `close` | no | Who may close an entry and open it again; as `change`. |
| `keep` | no | What is kept: `all` (the default); `member`, one entry per Member, where a new one replaces the old; `member-about`, one per Member about each entry; `age:<seconds>`, entries up to an age; `count:<number>`, the newest up to a number. |
| `about` | no | The kind of entry which an entry of this kind is about. Such an entry names the other when it is added, and goes when the other is removed. |
| `size` | yes | The largest content of an entry in bytes, at most `eds.data.max.inline.size`. Larger things are files, which an entry can name. |

post.description:
Unlocks EDS with the MasterKey after a restart, or sets a new MasterKey while no other Members exist.

**Fields:**

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `secret` | one of the two | The MasterKey secret, Base64-encoded. |
| `url` | one of the two | URL to read the secret from. |

Only the account `admin` may call this. The MasterKey is derived from the secret with
HKDF-SHA512; EDS stores only its version and a key check value (KCV), never the key
or the secret. The request has these outcomes:

- **First setup**: EDS is locked and no MasterKey was set up yet. The secret must
  meet the entropy rules; it becomes MasterKey version 1, and the System
  Administrator account is created if missing ("MasterKey unlocked").
- **Unlock**: EDS is locked (no source configured, or the source didn't match) and
  the secret matches the stored KCV. With valid System Administrator credentials,
  EDS is unlocked ("MasterKey unlocked"). A wrong secret is rejected by the KCV,
  without decrypting anything.
- **Same key**: EDS is unlocked and the secret gives the current MasterKey; only
  the stored URL is updated ("MasterKey unlocked").
- **Rotation**: EDS is unlocked and the secret gives a different MasterKey. The
  secret must meet the entropy rules. In one transaction, every value the MasterKey
  protects is re-wrapped with the new MasterKey, which gets the next version
  ("MasterKey updated"): the Members' salts and private keys and the Trustees'
  Circle Secrets. Sessions end, and pending invitations are deleted. Data Objects
  aren't touched, so a rotation is fast even with a lot of data.

When `url` is given, it is stored as `eds.masterkey.url` and used at the next start;
with `secret`, the stored URL is cleared. At startup, EDS reads the source from the
environment variable `EDS_MASTERKEY_URL`, the system property `eds.masterkey.url`,
or the setting, in that order. There is no default MasterKey: without a source,
EDS stays locked, and every other request fails with CRYPTO_ERROR until it is
unlocked.

Creates an invitation for a new Member, who then sets their own passphrase. An invitation always makes a user (STANDARD): a request with the role ADMIN is refused, as a link which falls into the wrong hands must not give more. An administrator is made by creating the account, or by changing the role afterwards.

**Fields:**

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `newAccountName` | yes | Up to 75 characters, unique. |
| `circleId` | for Members | The Circle the invited Member joins. Required unless the System Administrator invites. |
| `trustLevel` | no | `READ`, `WRITE` (default) or `ADMIN`, in the Circle. |
| `memberRole` | no | System Administrator only: `STANDARD` (default) or `ADMIN`. |
| `secret` | no | With a `circleId`: the invited Member's secret in the Circle, see `alterTrustee`. |

The System Administrator may invite anyone; other Members invite into a Circle they
administer. Returns the new account's ID in `memberId` and a one-time invitation
token in `invitation`. EDS stores only a keyed hash of the token, so it can't be
fetched again. The invitation expires after `eds.invitation.timeout.hours` (default
168), and becomes void if the MasterKey changes. While it is pending, the name can't
be invited again; once it has expired, a new invitation for the name replaces it.

With a `circleId`, the invited Member joins the Circle when accepting: the Circle's
key is sealed with a key derived from the token (HKDF-SHA512) and with the MasterKey,
so only the holder of the token can unlock it, and no one has to add the Member after
the acceptance. If the name already belongs to an account, it is added to the Circle
at once with `trustLevel`, and no invitation is returned.

invitation is accepted, or at once for an account which exists already. A client can
so hand the invited person a key of its own, wrapped with something only the two
share, without EDS being able to read it and without anyone having to be online when
the invitation is accepted.

To accept, the invited person sends a request to `updateMember` with
`credentialType` `INVITATION`, `accountName` set to the invited name,

get.description:
Returns the load and the inventory of the stone.

Returns the status of the stone: what it tells about itself to those who look after
it. The `Authorization: Bearer` header carries either a **status key** (see
`POST /status/keys`) or the session of the System Administrator. A status key reads
the status and nothing else, also while the stone is locked and waits for its
MasterKey; a session needs the stone to be awake.

Only general numbers are told: no names of Members, Circles or files, and nothing
about a single one of them.

| Query | Notes |
|---|---|
| `since` | Only samples of the load after this `sequence`: a client which asks often names the last sample it has and gets what is new. |
| `history` | `true` adds the load of the last 24 hours (`day`), and all kept samples of the inventory instead of the latest. |

The answer has the `name` of the stone (the setting `eds.stone.name`), its `version`,
whether it is `awake`, its `time` and when it `started`, the kind of `database`,
whether that is `persistent`, and a `databaseMark`: stones on the same database
server have the same mark, without the address being told. Then three series of
samples, the oldest first; each sample has a `sequence`, a `time` and `values`, numbers
by their names. A client shows the numbers it knows and passes over the others.

**`load`**: how busy the stone is. A sample is taken every `interval` seconds (the
setting `eds.status.load.interval.seconds`, default 5; 0 switches the gathering off),
and the last 720 are kept. Gathering reads counters and the Java runtime, so it is
cheap also every second; a request for the status gathers nothing.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `requests`, `failed` | Requests handled since the last sample, and those of them which were refused or failed. |
| `bytesIn`, `bytesOut` | Bytes received and sent with them, as far as the headers tell. |
| `requestMillis`, `requestMillisMax` | How long a request took: the average, and the longest. |
| `databaseMillis` | How long a trivial query to the database took, measured at most every 10 seconds. EDS can't read the load of the database; this rises with it. |
| `accounts` | Accounts with an authenticated request since the last sample. |
| `connections` | Open WebSocket connections. |
| `processShare` | The share of all processors which the stone's own process used since the last sample, 0 to 1. Left out where the platform doesn't tell. |
| `systemLoad`, `processors` | The load average of the host, and its processors. Two stones on one host tell the same; `processShare` tells them apart. |
| `memoryUsed`, `memoryMax` | Memory of the Java runtime, in bytes. |
| `threads` | Live threads. |

**`day`**: the load of the last 24 hours in steps of five minutes, the step still being
filled as the last. Counts are summed over the step; `requestMillis`, `databaseMillis`,
`processShare` and `systemLoad` are averages, with the peak as `<name>Max`; `accounts`,
`connections`, `memoryUsed` and `threads` are the highest of the step; `samples` is the
number of samples in it.

**`inventory`**: what the stone holds. Each number is a query, so a sample is taken
every `interval` seconds only (the setting `eds.status.inventory.interval.minutes`,
default 60), and the last 720 are kept.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `storageUsed`, `storageCeiling` | The stored, encrypted bytes, and the ceiling for them (`eds.data.max.total.size`). |
| `accounts`, `circles` | Accounts without the pending invitations, and Circles. |
| `files`, `entries` | Files, and entries of features. |
| `sessions` | Sessions which haven't expired. |
| `rotationsDue`, `rotationsRunning`, `rotationObjects` | Circles whose Circle Secret is due to be rotated and waits for a Trustee's request, those being rotated, and the Data Objects they still have to re-encrypt. |

All series are kept in memory and start anew with the stone.

A browser page from another address may call this, and the rest of the API, if the
setting `eds.cors.value` names its origin (several are separated by commas).

| 200 | `SUCCESS` | The request was completed. |
| 403 | `AUTHENTICATION_WARNING` | The Authorization header is missing, or it holds neither a status key nor a session which is known and hasn't expired. |
| 401 | `AUTHORIZATION_WARNING` | The session isn't the System Administrator's. |
| 406 | `VERIFICATION_WARNING` | The request is invalid: required fields are missing, values are too long or IDs are invalid. returnMessage lists the fields. |
| 591 | `CRYPTO_ERROR` | A key could not be unlocked, or another cryptographic operation failed. |
| 594 | `DATABASE_ERROR` | EDS is not ready (e.g. the database is invalid), or a database operation failed. |
| 500 | `ERROR` | An unexpected error occurred. |

post.description:
Changes a Trustee's trust level, their secret, or both.

**Fields:**

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `circleId` | yes | The Circle. |
| `memberId` | yes | The Trustee's Member ID. |

post.description:
Removes a Member from a Circle.

**Fields:**

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `circleId` | yes | The Circle. |
| `memberId` | yes | The Trustee's Member ID. |

Removes another Member from the Circle, which requires the trust level `ADMIN` in
the Circle (or the System Administrator), or removes the requesting Member, i.e.
leaves the Circle, which every Trustee may. The Member loses access to the Circle's
data at once; their open connections of the socket get `LEFT`. Even the last administrator may
leave; the System Administrator can then make another Trustee an administrator.
Afterwards the Circle Secret is rotated, so what the Member may have kept of it is of
no use (see `rotateCircle`).

The last Trustee of a Circle can neither leave nor be removed, not even by the System
Administrator: nobody could unlock the Circle's data afterwards. The Circle is deleted
instead.
